key_insight: Stacking ensemble learning achieved the best task-wise predictions for UTS, weld hardness, and HAZ hardness, while the multitask neural network offered strong shared-learning generalization across related welding outputs.
engineering_relevance: Accurate prediction of weld performance metrics can help optimize process settings, reduce destructive testing, and improve structural reliability in welded components.
method: Compared a multitask neural network (shared hidden layers with task-specific outputs) against stacking ensemble learning.
Predicted three welding properties simultaneously: UTS, weld hardness, and HAZ hardness.
Evaluated performance using RMSE and R² across the shared dataset.
evidence_signal: Stacking ensemble produced lower RMSE and higher R² for UTS and weld hardness, while both methods performed strongly on HAZ hardness, indicating task-dependent predictive strength.
watch_item: Results may depend on dataset size and task correlation; stacking can overfit if validation is not carefully separated and MTL may underperform when tasks are not strongly related.
paper_title: A Comparative Analysis of Multitask Neural Networks and Stacking Ensemble Learning for Predicting UTS, Weld Hardness, and HAZ Hardness in Welding Applications
